cases.title: A volcanic lead with a material contradiction
cases.subsite: Published VO193 locality, La Negra Formation (Mantos Blancos–Baquedano area)
cases.supported: Published local volcanic samples support questions about volcanic texture, material heterogeneity and sampling workflows within this regional terrain window.
cases.contradiction: The reported rocks include basaltic andesite and andesite. They do not establish a uniformly basaltic cell, pure basalt at the centre, lunar mare composition or regolith equivalence.
cases.scope: Reported literature points within the approximate 24 km DEM window; these are previously published localities, not new field discoveries. Exposure, access and positional error require verification.
cases.next_measurement: Verify exact exposure, material class and alteration at the intended station using permitted field logging, petrography and laboratory whole-rock analysis.

experiment.hypothesis: A rover-style observation protocol can document and test distinctions between local volcanic material classes and alteration, with disagreements retained.
experiment.objective: Rehearse geological observation and sampling; do not assume mare-material equivalence.
equipment: Petrography and whole-rock laboratory analysis with duplicates
procedure: Confirm access, permits and exposure before selecting stations.
Log ten accessible outcrops with coordinates, photographs and alteration descriptions.
Pre-register material classification rules and conduct duplicate laboratory comparisons.
experiment.success_indicator: Proposed completion criterion: ten complete georeferenced records and documented duplicate comparisons. Classification agreement is a result to measure, not an existing value.
experiment.unvalidated: No field survey, access approval, local material confirmation at proposed stations or experiment outcome exists.
experiment.cannot_reproduce: Lunar vacuum, gravity, radiation, regolith mechanics and space weathering.

cases.title: A sedimentary research question with a geographic evidence gap
cases.supported: Regional Makgadikgadi studies motivate investigation of playa sediments, groundwater and depositional processes. The candidate was selected algorithmically within this bounded search.
cases.contradiction: The reviewed regional studies do not verify a lacustrine section, carbonate unit, delta or biosignature-preservation site inside this cell. A published Mosu core is outside the DEM window. Regional Martian comparisons concern Meridiani/Arabia Terra, not demonstrated Jezero equivalence.
cases.scope: Keep the coordinate-based candidate identity. No named literature subsite within this terrain window was verified; measurements from other parts of the basin are not transferred.
cases.next_measurement: Acquire a local stratigraphic log and mineral identification to establish whether water-influenced deposits are actually exposed. Retain an inconclusive or negative result.

experiment.hypothesis: Accessible exposures within the candidate window may allow a rover-style test distinguishing aeolian and water-influenced depositional facies; this remains unestablished.
experiment.objective: Determine whether a local geological fieldwork hypothesis is supportable.
equipment: GNSS, scaled photography and field logs
procedure: Confirm permits, access and whether suitable exposures exist.
Record three georeferenced sections, grain size and sedimentary structures if available.
Compare independent facies classifications and preserve disagreements or insufficient exposure.
experiment.success_indicator: Proposed protocol-completion indicator: three documented station logs and independent classifications, or an explicit insufficient-exposure result. No expected mineral concentration or success probability is assumed.
experiment.unvalidated: No local mineralogical, lacustrine, carbonate or biosignature evidence has been established by this review.
experiment.cannot_reproduce: Martian gravity, atmospheric composition/pressure, radiation and ancient depositional history.
